item.title: Exact Solution of the $(2+1)$-Dimensional Dunkl-Klein-Gordon Oscillator with a Uniform Magnetic Field in Non-Commutative Phase Space
item.description: arXiv:2610.37820v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We solve the Klein-Gordon oscillator in a non-commutative phase space, generalized using Dunkl derivatives, both with and without interaction with a uniform magnetic field. For each of these cases, we begin by introducing the Dunkl derivative into the standard commutative phase space to evaluate the reflection parity symmetries. Then, using the Seiberg-Witten map, we extend the generalized system to a non-commutative phase space. In both cases, we determine the eigenfunctions and the energy spectrum exactly (which correspond to generalized Landau levels when a magnetic field is present). Furthermore, we compute the non-relativistic limit of the system and graphically analyze the behavior of the energy spectra. Our results demonstrate that the combination of the Dunkl deformation parameters, the non-commutative phase space geometry, and the magnetic field produces a parity-dependent modification of the energy levels. Finally, we verify that when the external magnetic field or the non-commutative parameters vanish, our exact solutions correctly reduce to the commutative Dunkl models established in previous works.
item.dc:creator: R. D. Mota, D. Ojeda-Guill\'en

item.title: Algebraic Quantum Field Theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.37904v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Algebraic quantum field theory describes a quantum system through its observables, their localisation in spacetime, and the states that assign them expectation values. The separation of the specification of observables from the choice of a state makes it possible to compare vacuum, thermal and charged representations without assuming that they share a preferred Hilbert space. We develop the framework from familiar quantum mechanics, construct the free scalar field, and explain how causality and positive energy constrain local measurements. The Reeh--Schlieder theorem, the structure of local von Neumann algebras and the split property reveal key differences between quantum theory in the continuum (i.e. QFT) and ordinary quantum mechanics with finitely many degrees of freedom. Superselection theory relates observable charges to statistics and internal symmetries. Finally, local covariance and perturbative and homological methods extend the discussion to curved spacetime, interactions and gauge theories. We also discuss measurement theory and quantum information aspects of AQFT.
item.dc:creator: Kasia Rejzner

item.title: From gauge-covariant Noether invariants to electromagnetic velocity-dependent mechanics
item.description: arXiv:2610.38128v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a charged particle, a spacetime symmetry need preserve the electromagnetic potential only up to a gauge transformation. Starting from the standard Noether--Bessel-Hagen construction, we make explicit the reduction from the relativistic gauge-invariant worldline charge to the generalized constants of nonrelativistic velocity-dependent mechanics, retaining the quasi-invariance boundary term throughout. With the convention $S_p=-mc\int ds+q\int A$, the canonical worldline one-form is $P=-m u^\flat+qA$, and a Killing vector satisfying $\mathcal L_XA=d\chi_X$ generates $C_X=P(X)-q\chi_X$. Its low-velocity limit is the Noether--Bessel-Hagen charge of the coordinate-time Lagrangian, from which generalized linear momentum, angular momentum and energy follow generator by generator. A uniform magnetic field gives an elementary gauge-dependent representative but gauge-invariant translational charge. The Darwin interaction then supplies the conservative $O(c^{-2})$ many-particle realization after field elimination, while a closed particle--field system is governed by the total stress-energy Killing charge. The result is an explicit reduction map linking three established descriptions without identifying their distinct conserved quantities.
item.dc:creator: A. S. de Castro

item.title: Homogenization theory of topological Anderson insulators: genuine gaps and pseudo-gaps
item.description: arXiv:2610.38150v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A topological Anderson insulator is an insulator whose non-trivial topological phase is induced by disorder. We develop a homogenization theory of this phenomenon for constant-coefficient elliptic systems perturbed by fluctuations oscillating at scale $\varepsilon$. Periodic fluctuations of every order below that of the operator, with appropriate amplitudes, do not average out: they produce an order-one correction $M$ given by a second-order (Born) formula, and the operator converges in the norm-resolvent sense to its homogenized limit. In particular, electric potentials and magnetic fields of zero mean, usually regarded as topologically trivial perturbations, generate corrections $M$ that change the topological phase. Fluctuations confined to a half-plane create an interface that carries the bulk-difference invariant of the homogenized operator for all $\varepsilon$ sufficiently small, a property that is stable under local defects. For random fluctuations, rare regions typically fill the homogenized gap, which becomes a pseudo-gap, and the standard interface index need no longer be defined. We define an index along cuts deformed so as to avoid the rare regions, and prove that it equals almost surely the bulk-difference invariant of the operator homogenized in the Born approximation, for first-order alloys with vanishing low moments and for a class of second-order systems with scalar disorder at criticality that includes the BHZ model.
item.dc:creator: Guillaume Bal

item.title: Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics of Semilinear Stochastic Partial Differential Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.38166v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a rigorous mathematical framework for the nonequilibrium thermodynamics of semilinear stochastic partial differential equations. The invariant Gaussian measure of the associated Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, which need not be time-reversible, serves as the reference measure. We define thermodynamic quantities in terms of probability densities and derive the entropy balance equation. We obtain explicit expressions for the entropy production rate and prove that its vanishing in the stationary state is equivalent to time reversibility. Sample-path entropy production is identified with the logarithm of the Radon-Nikodym derivative of the forward path measure with respect to the time-reversed path measure and is shown to satisfy fluctuation theorems. For nonstationary systems, sample-path entropy production decomposes into housekeeping heat and free-energy dissipation, each satisfying an integral fluctuation theorem. Both have nonnegative expectations, and the mean free-energy dissipation equals the decrease in relative entropy with respect to the stationary distribution. The theory is applied to semilinear stochastic heat equations with spatially correlated noise, a random polymer model, a nonlinear model with a divergence-free drift, and two coupled stochastic heat equations in contact with heat baths at different temperatures.
item.dc:creator: Zelin Liu, Hao Ge

item.title: Finite-volume and thermodynamic-limit lower bounds for the coherently driven Bose--Hubbard model via the Lieb--Yamazaki method
item.description: arXiv:2610.38464v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive rigorous lower bounds on the ground-state energy of the coherently driven Bose--Hubbard model using a Lieb--Yamazaki positive-operator decomposition. The resulting quadratic bounding Hamiltonian is diagonalized by displacement and Bogoliubov transformations, yielding explicit stability conditions and finite-volume bounds in arbitrary dimension. We establish the thermodynamic-limit energy density and characterize the excitation spectrum of the bounding Hamiltonian. We also derive its Gaussian-state observables, including filling, number fluctuations, and second-order correlations, and identify regimes of antibunching and sub-Poissonian statistics. Numerical calculations assess the tightness of the bounds across representative parameter regimes.
item.dc:creator: Maciej Janowicz, Joanna Kaleta, Filip Krzy\.zewski, Andrzej Zembrzuski

item.title: A Primer on Instanton Physics - A Short Course
item.description: arXiv:2610.38717v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: These six lectures, delivered at the University of New Brunswick 6-21 October 2026, are an introduction to instantons in quantum mechanics and quantum field theory for senior undergraduate and beginning graduate students. The first four lectures deal solely with particle mechanics, building the necessary background for the last two that cover applications in semi-classical field theory.
item.dc:creator: Pervez Hoodbhoy

item.title: From Entanglement Bootstrap to DHR Theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.38821v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a direct connection between the entanglement bootstrap and the Doplicher--Haag--Roberts theory of superselection sectors for two-dimensional quantum spin systems. Under the entanglement-bootstrap assumptions, we prove Haag duality and establish a one-to-one correspondence between simple entanglement-bootstrap anyon types and irreducible superselection sectors. For each fusion channel, we further construct an affine bijection from density matrices on the entanglement-bootstrap fusion space to normalized positive intertwiners in the corresponding operator-algebraic fusion channel. These results connect the entropic and operator-algebraic descriptions of anyons directly, without passing through exactly solvable lattice models.
item.dc:creator: Kohtaro Kato, Yoshiko Ogata

item.title: The geometry of Floquet states
item.description: arXiv:2610.38845v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies the moduli space of "good" periodic Hamiltonians, i.e., periodic Hamiltonians with nondegenerate Floquet spectrum. The corresponding Floquet states determine a geometric model for the moduli space of such Hamiltonians. The model is expressed in terms of configuration spaces, flag manifolds, and principal bundles. A corollary of the main result is the complete determination of the rational cohomology ring of the space of good periodic Hamiltonians. The paper also considers the adiabatic driving of a 1-parameter family of good periodic Hamiltonians. We formulate two conjectures describing the resulting asymptotic quantum evolution. These are Floquet analogues of the adiabatic theorem in quantum mechanics.
item.dc:creator: Vladimir Y. Cherynak, John R. Klein

item.title: A First-Order Phase Transition in Spin-Imbalanced BCS Theory of Superconductivity
item.description: arXiv:2610.38961v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a translation-invariant BCS functional of superconductivity for a system of spin-$1/2$ fermions with spin-dependent chemical potentials, $\mu_+\neq\mu_-$. Numerical work of Caldas and Mota and analytical work of Freiji, Hainzl, and Seiringer has suggested an unusual first-order phase transition in spin-imbalanced BCS models, in which the normal state becomes globally unstable while remaining locally stable. Here, we prove that a first-order phase transition occurs in such spin-imbalanced BCS functionals. For each sufficiently small fixed spin imbalance and sufficiently low temperature, there is a coexistence coupling $\lambda_{\mathrm{fo}}$ strictly below the linear-stability threshold $\lambda_{\mathrm{lin}}$ of the normal state at which the Cooper pair density exhibits a nonzero jump and the minimized energy has a kink. The methodological insight is a coercivity estimate obtained by decomposing the BCS energy minimization into two parts, where the ``inner'' problem minimizes over the one-particle density matrices at fixed pairing and can be exactly solved by a Legendre--Fenchel transform.
item.dc:creator: Marius Lemm, Barbara Roos

item.title: Minimally-coupled Quasilinear Symmetric Hyperbolic Systems, Naturally
item.description: arXiv:2610.39107v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider symmetric hyperbolicity and well-posedness in the context of natural equations, which are closed subobjects of jet bundles over natural bundles. We show how non-natural equations can be "naturalized", and we discuss how a precise version of "minimal coupling" offers a (provably unique, up to isomorphism) method for constructing natural equations from certain equations defined on a single manifold. We discuss how to define symmetrizers, hyperbolizations, and constraints for minimally coupled natural equations, and we show how these can be used to recover standard existence and uniqueness results, relative to any choice of background structure (a metric, for minimally coupled systems). Additionally, we show that minimal coupling and naturality together imply that the causal cones associated with a (first order, quasilinear, minimally coupled) naturally symmetric hyperbolic natural equation must always coincide with the metric lightcones, and that a certain rank-2 tensor, associates with a natural hyperbolization, must always be divergence free relative to the associated Levi-Civita derivative operator.
item.dc:creator: Eleanor March, James Owen Weatherall

item.title: Higher genus polylogarithms associated with the D'Hoker-Hidding-Schlotterer connection
item.description: arXiv:2610.39382v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study higher genus polylogarithms associated with the D'Hoker-Hidding-Schlotterer (DHS) connection defined on families of Riemann surfaces of any genus with marked points. Under separating degenerations of Riemann surfaces, we show that the DHS connection can be constructed by gluing the Brown-Levin (BL) connections on elliptic curves and the Knizhnik-Zamolodchikov (KZ) connections on pointed Riemann spheres. Therefore, the associated higher genus polylogarithms can be described explicitly as power series in deformation parameters and their logarithms for the families of Riemann surfaces whose coefficients are expressed by multiple zeta values and elliptic multiple zeta values.
item.dc:creator: Takashi Ichikawa

item.title: Generalized Frobenius Structures on Hurwitz Spaces, Their Open Extensions and Associated Principal Hierarchies
item.description: arXiv:2610.39411v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct generalized Frobenius structures on Hurwitz spaces of arbitrary genus using extended primary differentials. Through contour integrals involving the Cauchy kernel, we derive explicit dispersionless Lax representations for the principal hierarchies of these structures and their almost-dual counterparts. We also construct solutions to the open WDVV equations for both the original and almost-dual structures, and derive explicit principal hierarchies for the resulting rank-one extensions. Finally, we show that these constructions admit Shramchenko deformations.
item.dc:creator: Shilin Ma

item.title: Arithmetic localization for quasiperiodic long-range operators with monotone potentials
item.description: arXiv:2610.39448v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study one-dimensional quasiperiodic operators with $\alpha$-H\"older monotone potentials and long-range hopping satisfying $|T(x,y)|\leq \varepsilon e^{-\rho |x-y|}$. Under an explicit smallness condition on $\varepsilon$, we establish uniform Anderson localization for such operators in the regime $\rho>\alpha\beta $, where $\beta$ is the exponential strength of frequency resonances. Our proof extends the arithmetic localization strategy for monotone quasiperiodic Schr\"odinger operators by Jitomirskaya and Kachkovskiy to the long-range setting, without relying on the Lyapunov exponent.
item.dc:creator: Hongyi Cao

item.title: A Combinatorial Formula and a Hilbert Scheme Realization of a Rank-One Virasoro Irregular Conformal Block
item.description: arXiv:2610.39786v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For general central charge, we give a combinatorial formula and a geometric realization of the formal expansion of the rank-one Virasoro irregular conformal block of type $(0,0,1)$ at its irregular singular point. We realize the normalized block as a coefficientwise matrix element on the localized equivariant Hilbert--Fock space associated with Hilbert schemes of points on $\mathbb C^2$. At $c=1$, we prove the author's conjecture and express the parameter-independent coefficients in terms of skew-tableau numbers and Littlewood--Richardson coefficients, establishing their nonnegativity and integrality. The proof combines sectorial asymptotics of screening integrals with Laguerre--Jack evaluations. We express the screening kernel using the flow of a degree-raising differential operator and compute the Jack coefficients of its exponential from the one-box Pieri rule and the shifted Jack coefficient formula of Okounkov and Olshanski.
item.dc:creator: Hajime Nagoya

item.title: An Egorov-type Theorem for Analytic Wick Observables in Quantum Field Theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.39806v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide an exact Egorov-type formula, given by a convergent expansion in the semi-classical parameter $\varepsilon > 0$, for the propagation of a certain class of analytic Wick observables with super-exponentially decaying coefficients, under the action of a time-dependent quadratic Hamiltonian. This work generalizes a result established by S. Breteaux for polynomial symbols, and includes the spatially cutoff $P(\varphi)_2$ model, as well as a variant of the H\"oegh-Krohn model.
item.dc:creator: Julien Malartre

item.title: Three-dimensional stress-gradient non-locality problem: Displacement field for an arbitrary and a conservative force
item.description: arXiv:2610.39888v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In order to obtain the displacement field, both generally in the case of an arbitrary body force and specifically in the case of a conservative body force, the mechanical problem of statics of three-dimensional stress-gradient non-local medium is analytically solved on unbounded domain by considering a system of equations consisting of an equilibrium equation, infinitesimal strain, and both scalar- and tensor-type stress-gradient Eringen three-dimensional models. Since the system of equations is linear, for each model the solution is obtained in the form of a superposition of the local-type displacement field, common to each model, and the non-local-type displacement field, specific to the non-locality operator of the model. Among the three scalar-type and five tensor-type considered models, six distinct analytical displacement field expressions are obtained for an arbitrary body force: one expression specific to a scalar-type model, three specific to individual tensor-type models, while each of the remaining two expressions are common to one scalar- and one tensor-type model. The displacement vector fields are graphically represented in the case of gravitational body force, yielding five different models, since two tensor-type models become the same when the force is conservative.
item.dc:creator: Sla{\dj}an Jeli\'c, Du\v{s}an Zorica

item.title: Optimization Inverse Spectral Problems for Sturm--Liouville Operators with Potentials in $L^p(0,1)$
item.description: arXiv:2610.40231v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study an optimization inverse spectral problem (OISP) for a one-dimensional Sturm--Liouville operator on a finite interval. The problem is to find a potential $V \in L^p(0,1)$ that realizes a prescribed finite set $\lambda_1^* < \lambda_2^* < \dots < \lambda_m^*$ and has the smallest $L^p(0,1)$-distance from an a priori given potential $V_0 \in L^p(0,1)$. We formulate and prove results on the regularity of the isospectral manifold, the existence of an OISP solution, and an explicit analytic representation of the optimal potential by means of a power map applied to a linear combination of squared eigenfunctions. Using a unified differential-algebraic approach to squared eigenfunctions, we show that whenever these squares are linearly dependent, the corresponding potential can be expressed in terms of them and is an analytic function. For $p=2$, we prove that nondegenerate stationary points are isolated and that the number of global minima is finite provided that each of them is nondegenerate. For every $1<p<\infty$, we establish uniqueness for the first eigenvalue when $\lambda_1^*\ge\lambda_1(V_0)$ and generic global uniqueness in the sense of Baire category in $L^p(0,1)$. A separate section provides examples with at least two global minima for $m=1,2$ in the presence of a sufficiently high finite symmetric barrier. We describe an iteration with frozen eigenfunctions and a local Newton--KKT method with continuation in the spectral data, and state explicitly the limits of their guarantees. The final part discusses applications of OISP theory to nonlinear boundary value problems and to applied problems of diagnostics and optimal spectral design of acoustic and electromagnetic resonators.
item.dc:creator: Nur Valeev

item.title: Three-dimensional QCA that are not stably circuits
item.description: arXiv:2610.40235v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the three-dimensional chiral $\Z_p$ Clifford quantum cellular automata of Haah and of Sun--Yang--Wang--Tantivasadakarn--Chen are, for every odd prime $p$, not finite-depth quantum circuits, even after tensoring with arbitrary ancillary degrees of freedom and composing with translations. Previously such statements were known only inside the Clifford category. As a consequence, the group of three-dimensional QCA modulo stabilized circuits and translations is not finitely generated. The key ingredient is a new invariant of invertible subalgebras, which we conjecture to be the square of the total quantum dimension of the hosted anyon theory, modulo rational squares.
item.dc:creator: Bowen Yang

item.title: Bulk gap stability and spectral flow for fermions with weak long-range interactions
item.description: arXiv:2610.40299v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that weak long-range many-body interactions preserve the bulk gap of a free fermion system and that a quasi-local spectral flow transports the free ground state to ground states of the interacting system. Let $\Phi_h$ be a free fermionic interaction, possibly including pairing terms, whose infinite-volume Majorana coefficient operator $h$ has no spectrum in $(-g,g)$, and let $\mathcal V$ be an even self-adjoint many-body interaction. For sufficiently small $|\lambda|$, we construct pure ground states $\omega_{\lambda}$ of the interacting bulk system $\Phi_{\lambda}=\Phi_h+\lambda\mathcal V$ and quasi-local automorphisms $\beta_{0,\lambda}$ such that $\omega_{\lambda}=\omega_0\circ\beta_{0,\lambda}$, where $\omega_0$ is the free ground state of $\Phi_h$. Each $\omega_\lambda$ has a GNS Hamiltonian with gap at least $g-C_*|\lambda| \|\mathcal V\|_*$, where $\|\cdot\|_*$ is the relevant interaction norm. Our result allows polynomial decay of both the free coefficients and the many-body interaction. For two-site interactions on a uniformly discrete point set $\Gamma\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, a sufficient condition is decay as $(1+|x-y|)^{-\varpi}$ with $\varpi>2d$, for both the hopping and pairing coefficients and the interaction terms. The spectral-flow generator preserves the spatial exponent of the polynomial interaction norm, and its automorphisms satisfy locality bounds at that exponent. If $h$ and $\mathcal V$ have stretched-exponential decay, so does the spectral-flow generator. The proof constructs the spectral flow and establishes the gap through an excitation-number comparison, using polynomial propagation bounds for evolved interactions proved in a companion paper.
item.dc:creator: Stefan Teufel

item.title: Symmetries and exact solutions of stochastic differential equations: the CIR model
item.description: arXiv:2610.40316v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is well known that in the celebrated Cox-Ingersoll-Ross process for interest rates there exists a critical relation among the model parameters. In the present work, we explain this critical relation by studying the symmetries of the stochastic differential equation and compute the solution of the model using this symmetry. In this way we also recover results of a recent paper where this property has been studied within a broader context by analyzing the relationships among the symmetries of stochastic differential equations and their corresponding forward Kolmogorov equations.
item.dc:creator: Miguel A. Rodr\'iguez

item.title: Local determination of low-energy states in gapped fermion systems with weak long-range interactions
item.description: arXiv:2610.40337v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider bulk-gapped fermion systems whose infinite-volume bulk is obtained by adding sufficiently weak even many-body interactions to a free Hamiltonian with spectral gap $g>0$, allowing polynomial spatial decay of both parts. We prove quantitative local determination of low-energy states: whenever another interaction agrees with the bulk interaction inside a finite or infinite region $U$, with bulk terms crossing its boundary unchanged or removed, all its states with excitation energies in $[0,3g/4]$ have local expectations close to those of the bulk ground state deep inside $U$. The error decays with the distance to the complement of $U$, independently of the interaction terms supported outside $U$ and of the chosen low-energy state. Quantitative local determination has strong consequences. (i) The bulk interaction has a unique algebraic ground state. (ii) A strong "local perturbations perturb locally" (LPPL) principle holds: arbitrary distant defects change local ground-state expectations only by a spatially decaying error. (iii) Low-energy excitations in finite samples remain localized near the boundary for all times, up to spatially decaying tails, uniformly over arbitrary even boundary terms. (iv) Correlations from deep inside $U$ to outside $U$ are small, with quantitative bounds in terms of spatial separation and distance to $U^c$. To prove local determination of low-energy states, we combine quasi-adiabatic transport of the free ground state to the interacting bulk ground state with a new condition, local excitation detectability (LED). A companion paper establishes gap stability and constructs the transport for weak interactions, while we prove LED at sufficiently weak coupling. The abstract theorem is nonperturbative and applies whenever the transport and LED hypotheses hold.
item.dc:creator: Stefan Teufel

item.title: Twinor Theory: Field Equations from $(A)dS_4^{\mathbb C}$ Spin-Tractors: A Twin to Twistor Theory Modelled on $(A)dS_4^{\mathbb C}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.40435v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Twinor theory is formulated as a spacetime-based counterpart to twistor theory using holomorphic reductive Cartan geometry modelled on complexified $(A)dS_4$. The fundamental spin-tractor bundle defines Dirac twinors, its symmetric powers define ladder twinors, and their extremal Lorentz components define chiral twinors. The general \textit{twinor field equation} is $D\mathbf Y=\mathbf J$. Its adjacent contractions and mixed divergence are constrained by source relations; no additional equation is imposed on its completely symmetric projection. On a flat torsion-free Lorentzian background, the adjacent equations with the mass-normalization source and vanishing additional contracted sources, together with vanishing mixed divergence, reproduce the massive \textit{Dirac--Fierz--Pauli system}; the massless chiral realization gives the zero-rest-mass equations. Within the fixed mass normalization, the reality condition yielding a positive real mass squared is the \textit{anti-de Sitter reality condition} on the particle scale, independently of the cosmological scale and background curvature. The mass-coupling phase is therefore present in the classical connection before quantization. Nonlinear gravity is formulated through the full adjoint curvature, with energy--momentum and spin currents specifying Einstein--Cartan dynamics without requiring an action. The adjoint Bianchi identity constrains source compatibility, while a BGG-type sequence organizes torsion-free infinitesimal deformations. Matter interactions enter through the coupled connection and contracted source relations, with curvature compatibility recorded by $D\mathbf J=\mathcal F_D\mathbf Y$. Both chiralities are retained, and the additional consistency requirements for interacting higher-spin fields are distinguished from the underlying bundle construction.
item.dc:creator: Chen-Hsu Chien

item.title: Entropic Fluctuations in Quantum Statistical Mechanics: A Review
item.description: arXiv:2610.40463v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The celebrated Evans--Searles, respectively Gallavotti--Cohen, fluctuation theorem concerns certain universal statistical features of the entropy production rate of a classical system in a transient, respectively steady, state. In this paper, we review and compare several possible extensions of these fluctuation theorems to quantum systems. We present, in an introductory way, the approach proposed in a recent series of works [Lett. Math. Phys. 114, 32 (2024): doi:10.1007/s11005-024-01777-0], [Rev. Math. Phys 38, 2461006 (2026): doi:10.1142/S0129055X24610063], [Commun. Math. Phys. 406, 201 (2025): 10.1007/s00220-025-05360-z] and [J. Math. Phys. 67, 022101 (2026): doi:10.1063/5.0311182] including a previously missing extension of the Gallavotti--Cohen (steady state) version of the FT to two-time measurement entropy production in the algebraic setting of quantum dynamical systems. We focus on the open quantum systems, where a small system interacts with several (infinitely extended) reservoirs, and discuss the following approaches: naive, two-time measurement, phase space contraction and ancilla state tomography. We review the connection with modular theory. The latter provides a way to extend the classical notions to the quantum domain. We discuss the quantum version of the principle of regular entropic fluctuations, introduced in the classical context in [Nonlinearity 24, 699 (2011): doi:10.1088/0951-7715/24/3/003]. Finally, we relate the statistical properties of these various notions of entropy production to spectral resonances of quantum transfer operators and apply this approach to a paradigmatic model of non-equilibrium statistical mechanics: the spin-fermion model. The results presented here shed a new light on the nature of entropic fluctuations in quantum statistical mechanics.
item.dc:creator: Tristan Benoist, Laurent Bruneau, Vojkan Jak\v{s}i\'c, Aannalisa Panati, Claude-Alain Pillet

item.title: Gluons and Knots
item.description: arXiv:2610.10673v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We argue that the scattering amplitude of a single minus helicity gluon with arbitrarily many positive helicity gluons is topological. The amplitude is constant in chambers of kinematic space, its resonances are located at walls and its factorization is determined by wall-crossing. Yangian invariance dictates the amplitude to be determined by a 2d null Wilson loop that can be lifted into a positive and transverse 3d link. By reinterpreting wall-crossing and the Weinberg soft theorem as skein relations and Reidemeister moves of the subknots, we construct a state-counting description consisting of adding the `corners' of their HOMFLY-PT polynomials. Beyond the classical limit, we argue that this provides a conjectured but precise connection to topological field and string theory. The new formula is rigorously derived via a Lean-formalized dependency graph (DAG) as detailed in a companion paper, laying out the precise assumptions including Reidemeister III invariance. It is further tested exhaustively, including novel `star' kinematics where the amplitude and state count are shown to become Catalan numbers, in agreement with knot theory literature.
item.dc:creator: Alfredo Guevara

item.title: Nonlinear springs with orbits in radicals: a solvability criterion
item.description: arXiv:2610.37730v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: An odd polynomial oscillator has a periodic orbit given by a quadrature. When the zeros of the energy polynomial are all simple or all of even multiplicity, that quadrature is elementary exactly when the polynomial is a perfect square, and the time is a sum of inverse tangents. Recovering the displacement inverts that relation, algebraic when their coefficients are commensurate, making a closed form a Galois question. This paper identifies the group as the monodromy group of a rational map, computes its branch data from the parameters, and shows the branch value at the phase-angle singularity never vanishes, so every decomposition pairs the amplitudes reciprocally. In the commensurate family with distinct real factors, the orbit is radical exactly when the primitive inversion degree is at most four, or when reciprocal pairs leave a reduced spring of that degree. Radical orbits occur at the fifth, ninth, thirteenth and seventeenth force orders, the last only for reciprocal members, an expression recorded for each. The multiplicity hypothesis cannot be dropped. Factoring the energy polynomial into square and squarefree parts turns the quadrature into a differential of the third kind on a hyperelliptic curve, where elementarity is a torsion condition on the divisor of its poles with a vanishing holomorphic remainder. The first nonsquare elementary member appears at the ninth force order, and the power pullback inverts in closed form at every such order, giving a radical orbit for a confining spring of arbitrarily high degree with a sufficient condition for positive coefficients.
item.dc:creator: Unnikrishna Pillai

item.title: Defining 2-group symmetries on lattices and extracting their anomalies
item.description: arXiv:2610.37745v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Ordinary $0$-form symmetries $G$ can mix with $1$-form symmetries $\Pi_2$ to form a $2$-group $\mathcal{G}$. We give a concrete lattice definition for a class of finite $2$-group symmetries in terms of local relations among symmetry operators. These relations identify the Postnikov class $[\rho]\in H^3(BG,\Pi_2)$ that characterizes the mixing. We develop a method to extract anomalies of these symmetries in one spatial dimension by restricting symmetry operations to an interval and comparing their composition near its endpoints. We also construct explicit qubit symmetry actions in $d=1,2,3$ spatial dimensions for a $2$-group with $G=\Pi_2=\mathbb{Z}_2$. These actions share the same nontrivial Postnikov class but include both anomaly-free and anomalous realizations. Their cohomological anomalies are classified by $H^{d+2}(B\mathcal G,U(1))$, which is $\mathbb{Z}_2$ for $d=1,2$ and $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2$ for $d=3$, and our constructions realize every class in these dimensions. Our results connect higher-group symmetry and its anomalies to concrete lattice operations, providing a microscopic framework for studying anomalous symmetries.
item.dc:creator: Yitao Feng, Yu-An Chen

item.title: Fundamental limits on photonic state preparation from phase-space majorization
item.description: arXiv:2610.37755v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Preparing complex quantum states of light for quantum information processing tasks often proceeds by converting from simpler states via experimentally accessible operations. We provide fundamental bounds on such probabilistic conversions, both exact and approximate. To do so, we establish a theory of weak, fully relative majorization that compares the disorder of phase-space functions. Our framework is versatile and can be tailored to different systems and sets of allowed operations. Focusing on Wigner functions in multimode photonic systems, we establish rigorous no-go results and tradeoff relations for exact and approximate conversions involving squeezed states, cat states, Gottesman--Kitaev--Preskill states, and Fock states. In doing so, we derive novel bounds and recover known tight ones. Our results demonstrate that phase-space disorder imposes strong limitations on photonic state preparation.
item.dc:creator: Twesh Upadhyaya, Oliver Hahn, Ulysse Chabaud, Nikolaos Koukoulekidis

item.title: Characteristic identities for orthogonal quantum matrices: examples
item.description: arXiv:2610.37813v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this note, we illustrate our recent results regarding structure theory of orthogonal Quantum Matrix algebras \cite{OP-BMW,OP-reciprocal,OP-ortho} using the simplest nontrivial example: the RTT-algebra associated with the canonical orthogonal R-matrix of type $O(3)$ (see, e.g., \cite{FRT}). By introducing a suitable linear order on the set of generators, we obtain a set of quadratic relations defining the algebra. Next, we investigate relations among its higher-degree polynomials. As a result, we verify `in components' the Cayley-Hamilton and the reciprocal relations, obtained earlier with the use of the R-matrix techniques. We explicitly calculate the coefficients of the characteristic polynomials of quantum matrices and propose a conjecture regarding the form of the Hilbert-Poincar\'e series for the RTT-algebra.
item.dc:creator: Oleg Ogievetsky, Pavel Pyatov

item.title: Stellar Representation of Gottesman Kitaev Preskill States on the Double Discrete Cylinder
item.description: arXiv:2610.37831v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Covariant integral quantization is developed on the double discrete cylinder phase space, with the torus as configuration space, and yields the Wigner distribution and the stellar representation. This phase space is particularly well suited to translationally invariant states, such as the Gottesman Kitaev Preskill (GKP) states. These states are central to fault-tolerant quantum computing architectures, yet their quantum resources are still under investigation. The stellar representations of ideal GKP logical states, which behave as phase eigenstates of the double discrete cylinder, have no zeros on this phase space, whereas those of their superpositions have infinitely many. The vacuum, although Gaussian, has zeros on this phase space, and the zeros of finitely squeezed GKP states move with the widths of the peaks and of the envelope, and reach this phase space for fine-tuned widths. These features echo the role of the vacuum as the resource that makes GKP-based architectures hard to simulate.
item.dc:creator: Aidan Zlotak, Nicolas Fabre, Romain Murenzi

item.title: The Geometry of Quantum Teleportation in Phase Space
item.description: arXiv:2610.37861v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We formulate the standard quantum teleportation protocol within the framework of deformation quantization, employing the Stratonovich--Weyl (SW) correspondence and the associated star product on the coadjoint orbits of $SU(2)$. Each qubit is represented by a spherical phase space $S^2$ endowed with the Kirillov--Kostant--Souriau (KKS) symplectic structure. Within this setting, we explicitly construct the phase space representations of the entangled Bell resource, the controlled-NOT and Hadamard operators, the projective measurements, and the conditional Pauli corrections. We demonstrate how the quantum information initially encoded in the Wigner function for the input qubit is redistributed through bipartite and tripartite phase space correlations. Upon consideration of a conditional unitary transformation, the measurement outcome produces a Wigner function on the receiver's coadjoint orbit that is related to the input by an outcome-dependent rotation, which can subsequently be inverted through the implementation of an appropriate Pauli correction. The covariance of the SW correspondence provides a geometric interpretation of this process, in which quantum information is redistributed and reconstructed without transferring the underlying symplectic geometry. Our formulation can also be extended to study quantum teleportation in more general phase space geometries equipped with suitable star products.
item.dc:creator: Jasel Berra-Montiel, Alberto Molgado, Mar S\'anchez-C\'ordova

item.title: Hierarchical Laminates Cannot Reproduce All Effective Properties of Planar Two-Phase Composites: A Counterexample with a 16-Component Potential
item.description: arXiv:2610.37899v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Designing a composite requires understanding which effective properties can be achieved through varying its microstructure, i.e., the spatial arrangement of given constituent materials. Hierarchical laminates, created by successive layering, reach many known limits on these properties, making it natural to ask whether they can reproduce every effective response obtainable from the same constituents. We answer this question negatively for planar two-phase composites governed by linear systems whose potentials have 16 or more components. We construct constituent material properties and, at any prescribed nontrivial phase fraction, periodic microstructures whose effective properties cannot be approximated by hierarchical laminates, even when layer directions, proportions, and the number of layering steps are unrestricted. We design the constituents so that all hierarchical laminates have equal effective energies at two prescribed mean gradients. The key step is to construct a medium whose local properties are those of horizontal laminates with smoothly varying phase fractions, but whose effective energies violate this equality. Approximating these energies with sufficiently fine periodic stripes of the original constituents yields the two-phase counterexample. This construction also gives a negative answer to the two-well relaxation problem: the minimum of two positive-definite homogeneous quadratic forms on $\mathbb{R}^{2\times32}$ can have distinct quasiconvex and rank-one convex envelopes. The counterexample and the strict inequality between the envelopes are formally verified in Lean 4.
item.dc:creator: Lianghao Cao

item.title: An Integral Equation for the Surface Current in the Problem of the Natural Modes of a Waveguide Containing a Resistive Film
item.description: arXiv:2610.37907v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper considers the eigenmode problem for a waveguide with a resistive film. An integral equation for the surface current on the film is formulated. A method for evaluating the kernel is described, and an explicit expression for the kernel is derived for rectangular and circular waveguides.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Soviet Journal of Communications Technology and Electronics, vol. 31, no. 2, pp. 33-39, February 1986
item.dc:creator: I. M. Braver, Kh. L. Garb, P. Sh. Fridberg

item.title: Diffraction of rotated measures
item.description: arXiv:2610.37992v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Consider a translation-bounded measure on the line. We can rotate the measure, distributing the mass proportionally to the area, to create a two-dimensional rotationally invariant translation-bounded measure. We show that the diffraction of the two-dimensional object is the normalised rotation of the diffraction of the original measure. We discuss some examples and generalisation beyond $d=2$.
item.dc:creator: Jan Maz\'a\v{c}, Nicolae Strungaru

item.title: Systematic High Overtone Expansion of Kerr Quasinormal Modes
item.description: arXiv:2610.38019v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a systematic method to compute the high overtone expansion of Kerr quasinormal modes on normal angular branches to arbitrary order. We first obtain the expansion of the angular eigenvalue at large frequencies by a simple polynomial recursion. Using this result in an alternative form of the radial Teukolsky equation, we find that all the WKB corrections are defined on a fixed genus-one spectral curve, and that the quantum periods at the second and higher orders are expressed in terms of only two elliptic periods. This allows us to determine the expansion coefficients order by order. We confirm that the truncated expansions reproduce quasinormal frequencies obtained by solving the angular and radial equations directly, for scalar, electromagnetic and gravitational fields. We also compare the scalar results with the exact WKB analysis of extremal Kerr black holes.
item.dc:creator: Yasuyuki Hatsuda

item.title: Hybrid CutFEM-IFEM model for embedded and immersed interfaces with triply-cut cells for the 2D Poisson problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.38271v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a hybrid CutFEM--IFEM method for 2D Poisson problems with an immersed fluid--fluid interface and an embedded fluid--solid interface on a single unfitted mesh. The proposed method leverages the strengths of both unfitted finite element methods and immersed interface techniques to handle complex interface geometries and strong discontinuities efficiently. A composite equivalent polynomial representation of the Heaviside and Dirac delta functions is used to integrate on triply-cut cells. Moreover, the IFEM basis functions are enriched with the lift functions exactly representing solution and flux jumps. Numerical examples show optimal convergence for linear and quadratic elements, with accuracy comparable to that of a mesh fitted to both interfaces.
item.dc:creator: Darsh Nathawani, Christopher Kees

item.title: Genericity of singularities of solutions to quasilinear systems on compact sets
item.description: arXiv:2610.38370v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the genericity of singularities of types $A_2,A_3,D_4^\pm$ in solutions of the equations of gas dynamics and nonlinear geometrical optics. The sets of solutions satisfying the corresponding transversality conditions are proved to be open and dense in spaces of smooth and real-analytic solutions equipped with the Whitney topology on compact sets.
item.dc:creator: Azamat Shavlukov

item.title: Electromagnetic Potentials via the Extended Maxwell System
item.description: arXiv:2610.38500v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct electromagnetic potentials on arbitrary open 3-dimensional sets for anisotropic, non-homogeneous materials, thus rendering any topological assumption like simple connectedness or the absence of holes superfluous in this context. The main idea is to invoke the extended Maxwell system the easy solution theory of which then yields existence of both scalar- and vector potentials.
item.dc:creator: Rainer Picard, Sascha Trostorff, Marcus Waurick

item.title: Nonlinear response and retarded three-point correlators of charge transport
item.description: arXiv:2610.38571v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study nonlinear response of charge transport in relativistic kinetic theory within the relaxation time approximation. For a classical gas of massless charged particles coupled to an external $U(1)$ gauge field, we organize the Boltzmann equation perturbatively in the source and derive a recursive solution for the distribution function to arbitrary response order. At second order we analytically obtain fully retarded three-point correlators at generic frequencies and momenta, verify the Ward identities implied by charge conservation. We also discuss the general properties of these correlators, including their analytic structure, consistency limits, and relation to Schwinger--Keldysh effective theories of diffusive fluctuations.
item.dc:creator: Jin Hu

item.title: Resurgence and Modularity in the First Painlev\'e Equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.38584v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For the first Painlev\'e equation, we relate three nonlinear Stokes maps associated with a full turn around infinity to modular transformations of the two-parameter tau function through the identity $\boldsymbol S_\pi\circ\boldsymbol S_0\circ \boldsymbol S_{-\pi}=\mathsf S\circ\mathsf T$. Here the subscripts label Borel directions, while $\mathsf S$ and $\mathsf T$ denote the modular generators. Working under the analytic assumptions of the topological recursion and exact WKB constructions, we compare Stokes multipliers of the associated isomonodromy system while tracking the homology basis of its elliptic spectral curve under rotations of the independent variable. For the sectors considered, we identify the known parameter transformation induced by an $8\pi/5$ rotation with the modular $T$-action and derive a new explicit parameter relation realizing the $S$-action for a $2\pi/5$ rotation. We also determine the multiplicative factors in the corresponding tau-function relations, including their normalization constants. Together, these results give an explicit realization of single-valuedness after one full turn around infinity for both the Painlev\'e transcendent and its tau function, with the tau-function prefactors cancelling by Abel's five-term identity for the Rogers dilogarithm.
item.dc:creator: Kohei Iwaki, Noam Tamarin

item.title: Inhomogeneous Geometric Last Passage Percolation and the $q$-deformed Jacobi Unitary Ensemble
item.description: arXiv:2610.38646v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study directed last passage percolation with geometric weights in a spatially inhomogeneous environment. We derive an explicit limit shape and establish fluctuation limits for the passage time, showing that, depending on the strength of the inhomogeneity, the limiting fluctuations are governed by Fredholm determinants associated with either the Airy or Bessel kernel. Our approach is based on an exact relation between the passage time and the smallest particle of the $q$-deformed Jacobi unitary ensemble ($q$-JUE). As part of our analysis, we derive the macroscopic limiting density of the $q$-JUE, which provides a natural $q$-deformation of the classical Wachter distribution, as well as of the limiting distribution of the Meixner ensemble. We further establish Airy and Bessel scaling limits for the smallest particle, which are of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Sung-Soo Byun, Yeong-Gwang Jung, Nick Simm

item.title: Goldbach Representations in Quantum Optics and Metrology
item.description: arXiv:2610.38675v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We derive a relation between Goldbach representations and photon-number statistics in a quantum-optical setup. Considering an even-number Fock state injected into a stochastic beam splitter with uniformly distributed transmissivity and projections of the two output modes onto prime subspaces, we demonstrate that each successful outcome corresponds to an Goldbach representation and that the averaged detection probability is exactly proportional to the number of Goldbach representations. Then, employing the Hardy--Littlewood asymptotic formula, we demonstrate that the post-measurement state generated by a beam splitter with fixed transmissivity exhibits standard quantum limit scaling of the ultimate precision limit in terms of phase estimation, whereas an equally weighted superposition of Goldbach representations exhibits Heisenberg scaling. These results provide a quantum-optical realization of Goldbach representations and relate their statistics of with quantum metrology.
item.dc:creator: Akira Sone, Maxim Olshanii

item.title: The Effective Field Theory Origin of the Fuzzy Sphere Method
item.description: arXiv:2610.38702v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Fuzzy sphere Hamiltonians for (2+1)D conformal field theories are usually written directly on the lowest Landau level. We introduce a framework organizing them as descendants of local ``mother theories'' on $S^2\times\mathbb R$. We start with the example of Ising mother theory built from two charged Dirac fermions coupled to a real mediator $\phi$. Integrating out $\phi$ and the higher Landau levels produces the fuzzy Hamiltonian, while integrating out the fermions gives a conventional local $\phi$ effective field theory flowing to the Ising point. Mild modifications of the same theory reach the Gaussian point (tricritical route) and the Lee-Yang continuation. Exploring the space of mother theories, we next promote $\phi$ to a complex field $\Phi$ and construct a new example, whose descendant is an easy-plane ferromagnet on the fuzzy sphere. Its spontaneous symmetry breaking phase gives a pseudo-Goldstone relativistic scalar, similar to the model introduced by Y.-C. He, while its critical point is non-relativistic, providing the first example of $z=2$ scaling on the fuzzy sphere. Remarkably, it admits exact one-magnon solutions, and the $z=2$ critical point can be found analytically. We then outline a rich landscape of further applications of our approach.
item.dc:creator: Mykola Dedushenko

item.title: Regional accuracy of physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) for recirculation in a deep lid-driven cavity
item.description: arXiv:2610.38814v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deep lid-driven cavities contain strong motion beneath the lid and much weaker recirculation at depth, so agreement in bulk velocity is an incomplete assessment of a computed flow. We examine data-free physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) for steady, two-dimensional incompressible flow in a cavity of depth-to-width ratio five at Reynolds numbers 100, 250, 500 and 1000. An established hard-constrained streamfunction formulation is combined with prescribed regional collocation, transferred initialization, and selected residual-scaling and envelope variants. Independent spectral/$hp$ calculations with the same Gaussian-regularized lid provide the reference fields. For a cavity of depth-to-width ratio $D/W=5$ at Reynolds numbers $\mathrm{Re}=100$, 250, 500, and 1000, evaluation on a common $121\times605$ grid gives interior relative velocity discrepancies of 5.130\%--7.850\%. Over the same cases, floor-region relative velocity discrepancies remain below 5\%, with absolute RMS discrepancies ranging from $1.255\times10^{-10}U$ to $2.332\times10^{-9}U$, where $U$ is the lid-velocity scale. In a separate $161\times801$ assessment at $\Rey=1000$, the refined workflow lowers interior velocity discrepancy from 5.624\% to 2.658\% and gauge-aligned pressure RMS discrepancy from $2.793\times10^{-3}$ to $1.167\times10^{-3}\rho U^2$. The improvements compare accumulated training workflows and do not isolate regional sampling. Configuration rankings depend on both region and observable. These finite-budget comparisons establish where the retained workflows agree with the reference and where rotational-field discrepancies remain substantial.
item.dc:creator: Ehsan Roohi, Christopher J. McDevitt

item.title: Generalized Symmetries of QED$_4$ on Non-Spin Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.38907v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generalized symmetries are sensitive to the tangential structure of spacetime. We study this interplay for massless QED on oriented non-spin four-manifolds, where the photon becomes a spin$^c$ connection and the path integral sums over spin$^c$ structures. The shifted flux quantization extends the magnetic 1-form symmetry into a $w_2$-twisted 1-form symmetry: its $2\pi$ rotation acts as a gravitational sign, fixed by the normal bundle of the surface the operator wraps. The obstruction to treating it as an ordinary magnetic 1-form symmetry is an order-two mixed magnetic-gravitational anomaly, which is classified by reduced oriented bordism and detected on the Wu manifold. In a fixed spin$^c$ sector, this anomaly is removable by a counterterm, so it is a property of the sum over spin$^c$ structures. We discuss its consequences for gapped, Coulomb, and Higgs phases. The chiral anomaly is governed by the index of the spin$^c$ Dirac operator, so rational chiral defects carry gravitational as well as electromagnetic responses. A spin$^c$ Hall topological field theory cancels the electromagnetic part but leaves a framing anomaly. At the level of anomaly inflow, this is canceled for every rational angle by stacking a neutral, generally noninvertible Witten-Reshetikhin-Turaev layer. The same framing subtlety affects the chiral defects of QED on curved spin manifolds. The complex projective plane illustrates each of these features explicitly.
item.dc:creator: Michele Del Zotto, Vivek Saxena

item.title: A Note on the Smoluchowski Coagulation-Fragmentation Equation with Fractional Laplacian
item.description: arXiv:2610.38908v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this work, we assess the well-posedness of the Smoluchowski coagulation-fragmentation equation with fractional Laplacian. In particular, we consider a truncated set of discrete Smoluchowski-type equations modeling the formation of clusters, with homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions, where the diffusive term describes a non-standard behavior in the movement of particles ('anomalous' diffusion).
item.dc:creator: Mattia Cantoni, Silvia Lorenzani

item.title: Hydrodynamic and Dynamical Phi^4 Limits of Ising-Kac Models with Diffusion-Based Interactions on the Sierpi\'nski Gasket
item.description: arXiv:2610.38982v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a general form of Ising--Kac interactions through heat-kernel averaging, with the heat-time parameter replacing the role of the interaction range. From the viewpoint of Dirichlet forms theory, this construction provides an intrinsic analogue of the mesoscopic averaging in classical Kac models when translation invariance is unavailable. We then investigate limits of this model on graph approximations of the Sierpi\'nski gasket. For the associated Glauber dynamics, we establish a hierarchy of scaling limits for the magnetization field. First, at fixed interaction heat time and inverse temperature, we derive a nonlocal hydrodynamic equation on the continuum gasket. Second, as the heat time vanishes and the inverse temperature approaches its mean-field critical value, suitably rescaled hydrodynamic solutions converge to the solution of the deterministic Allen--Cahn equation. Finally, under a joint scaling of graph refinement, interaction heat time, and inverse temperature near criticality, we prove convergence of critical magnetization fluctuations to the solution of the dynamical $\Phi^4$ equation. These results provide a concrete realization of the Ising-$\Phi^4$ correspondence in a geometric setting with non-integer spectral dimension.
item.dc:creator: Hongyi Chen, Seoyeon Yang

item.title: An Autonomous Spectral Representation for Fully Asymmetric Spherical Sherrington-Kirkpatrick Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.39115v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the large size dynamics of a fully asymmetric spherical Sherrington- Kirkpatrick model, allowing for a distinguished random signal that interacts with the evolving spin configuration. We first derive the large-N dynamical mean-field limit and characterize the law of a typical coordinate by an effective Gaussian process whose covariance must satisfy a self-consistency relation. The resulting formulation is intrinsically nonlocal in time and is not, in its usual form, a closed finite-dimensional dynamical system. Our main contribution is an autonomous spectral representation of this limiting dynamics. We introduce an auxiliary stationary chain of Gaussian replicas whose one-step marginal reproduces the effective field appearing in the dynamical mean- field equation. Applying a matrix-valued Herglotz representation, or equivalently Fourier analysis in the replica index, converts the covariance structure of the chain into a family of finite-dimensional matrix-valued evolution equations indexed by the unit circle. The macroscopic observables, including the signal overlap, are then recovered from explicit spectral integrals. This representation replaces the original two-time self-consistency problem by an autonomous spectral closure and provides a convenient framework for both analysis and numerical computation. We prove the validity of the representation and compare its predictions with direct simulations of the finite-dimensional system
item.dc:creator: James MacLaurin, Pedro Vilanova

item.title: Beyond energy bounds: comparing Schr\"odinger eigenstates
item.description: arXiv:2610.39136v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We derive eigenstate comparisons from ordered Schr\"odinger operators, extending energy bounds to overlaps, spatial distributions and nodes. For three form-ordered operators with discrete comparison ground states, suppose the upper ground-state energy lies in the lower operator's ground-state gap. Three comparison spectral values then bound all three squared ground-state overlaps and guarantee a simple discrete intermediate ground state. Related gap estimates control low-energy subspaces and individual excited-state overlaps under additional gap conditions. In one dimension and radially, a single crossing of the potential difference relative to the energy shift orders ground-state likelihood ratios and monotone observables; a nondecreasing difference suffices. The results cover asymmetric wells and shortened right Dirichlet walls, with coordinatewise comparisons for submodular reference potentials and coordinatewise nondecreasing perturbations. A two-sided Sturm argument orders corresponding internal nodes for nondecreasing potential differences, even between orthogonal one-dimensional excited states. For Yukawa ground states, Hulth\'en comparisons bound overlaps, radial moments and the density at the nucleus; the latter two-sided bounds hold for screening $0<\delta<2/\sqrt6$. Optimizing scaled Hulth\'en majorants gives a lower bound of approximately $1.13611$ for $n^2\delta_c(n,0)$, where $\delta_c(n,0)$ is the critical screening for the $n$th $s$-wave bound state. This bound is optimal within that two-parameter comparison family.
item.dc:creator: Xiao-Ke Wang, Han Jia, Shengjun Wu, Zeng-Bing Chen

item.title: Irreducible representations of $SU(3)$ for nucleons in a oscillator shell $\eta$ with $\eta \le 8$: Application to nuclei with proxy-$SU(4)$ symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2610.39357v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Applying some simple rules, established in group theory literature, generated are codes (easy to modify as required) for obtaining $SU(3)$ irreducible representations (irreps) for a given number of nucleons in a given oscillator shell $\eta$ with $\eta \le 8$. In this approach, first the $SU(3)$ irreps are obtained for spinless fermions in a given $\eta$ shell. Using the codes developed, tables of $SU(3)$ irreps are generated for identical nucleons (protons or neutrons) with a given total spin $S$. Similarly, the $SU(3)$ irreps are generated for nucleons with a given spin-isospin $SU(4)$ irrep. Some applications of these tables for $\eta=4$ shell for $52 \le \mbox{Z,N} \le 78$ nuclei with proxy-$SU(4)$ symmetry are presented. Also, the procedure used for the shell model $SU(3)$ limits is easy to be extended for the $SU(3)$ limit of various interacting boson models and some examples for these are also presented.
item.dc:creator: V. K. B. Kota

item.title: Analytic Solutions To Fully Quantized Parametric Amplification
item.description: arXiv:2610.39387v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We derive analytic expressions for observable dynamics under the fully quantized trilinear Hamiltonian, governing quantum three-wave mixing and parametric amplification. Starting from a coherent pump and vacuum signal and idler, the calculation reorganizes the Heisenberg expansion into resummed depletion and return profiles, yielding directly evaluable expressions for all 1st-, 2nd- and 3rd-order correlations. The construction uses no parametric approximation or fitted parameters. Representative numerical benchmarks show errors of order $10^{-12}$ throughout the entire pump depletion, and below $10^{-3}$ across dozens of depletion-and-back-conversion cycles, up to the first total collapse of the oscillation. The first-depletion treatment additionally provides 4th-order correlations, accommodates bright squeezed-pump inputs and reveals phenomena important to future optical quantum technologies. The framework can be extended to higher moments.
item.dc:creator: Wanli Xing, Timothy C. Ralph

item.title: P\"oschl-Teller type of Jaynes-Cummings Hamiltonians: SUSY transformations
item.description: arXiv:2610.39401v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The aim of this work is to define and investigate the generalized Jaynes-Cummings (JC) Hamiltonian by means of supersymmetric (SUSY) quantum mechanics methods. We have considered trigonometric and hyperbolic P\"oschl-Teller (PT) potentials as two natural ingredients to modify the standard JC model. We show that these generalized JC Hamiltonians have a list of characteristics in common with the JC Hamiltonian, for example: matrix intertwining, excitation number symmetry, Rabi frequency, formulas for atomic inversion and classical and revival times. Therefore, we conclude that JC Hamiltonians can be considered as one example of a wider a class of generalized Hamiltonians which can be useful in broader interaction problems.
item.dc:creator: \.{I}smail Burak Ate\c{s}, \c{S}eng\"ul Kuru, Javier Negro, Efe Serbest

item.title: Covariant phase space analysis of static spherical vacua in power-law $f(R)$ gravity
item.description: arXiv:2610.39484v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We formulate the static, spherically symmetric vacuum equations of power-law metric $f(R)$ gravity as a covariant autonomous system using the $(1+1+2)$ formalism. The finite critical sets include the scale-invariant Clifton--Barrow solution, a Minkowski endpoint shared by the Schwarzschild family, and degenerate boundaries of the normalized chart. The Clifton--Barrow equilibrium is an outward-radial attractor over a positive interval of the power-law parameter, whereas the Schwarzschild endpoint is a saddle of the polynomially extended system. Poincar\'e compactification, supplemented by secondary and weighted charts, resolves several asymptotic regimes. In particular, normally attracting sheets at large normalized curvature occur in the positive-curvature sector and are separated from the negative-curvature Clifton--Barrow equilibrium. Metric reconstruction also identifies a selected scalar-flat family with a regular throat, one asymptotically flat end, and a curvature-singular end. These results organize the regular reduced chart and the boundary regimes resolved here; they do not constitute a complete classification of static spherical vacua. All stability statements concern the static radial flow.
item.dc:creator: Mariam Campbell, Eduardo Bittencourt, Peter K. S. Dunsby

item.title: It\^o versus Stratonovich for shot noise with state-dependent amplitude: why the answer is Marcus
item.description: arXiv:2610.39511v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For Gaussian white noise the It\^o and Stratonovich prescriptions differ by $O(dt)$ per time step, which accumulates into the familiar spurious drift $\tfrac12 D\,II'$. We show that for renewal shot noise with state-dependent gain, $\dot x=-C(x)-I(x)\xi[t]$ with $\xi[t]$ a train of Dirac spikes of finite random amplitude, the two prescriptions differ by a finite amount at every event, and that where $I$ vanishes the difference can become qualitative. The Marcus kick, the jump-process counterpart of the Stratonovich prescription, is the flow map of $dx/ds=I(x)$: no kick can cross a zero $x^\ast$ of $I$, for any jump and waiting-time statistics. The It\^o kick is only the tangent map of that flow. For $I(x)=1+\beta x$ it crosses $x^\ast=-1/\beta$ if and only if $\xi\beta>1$ and collapses the whole line onto $x^\ast$ at $\xi\beta=1$; below threshold it is itself a Marcus kick with a remapped jump law. Bounded jump laws thus have a threshold, while unbounded ones leak across the barrier for \emph{any} parameters. The discrepancy cannot be absorbed into a renormalised drift beyond lowest order, and only the Marcus kick is generated by a single operator, which makes the master equation of Bianucci, Bologna and Mannella (2026) intrinsically Marcus. Numerically, the standard Heun kick is a second-order truncation of the Marcus map that preserves the barrier only because its order is even; it shortens every jump, biasing second moments in proportion to the squared jump amplitude and the jump kurtosis, and depleting the region near the barrier. We give the exact-flow integrator that replaces it.
item.dc:creator: Marco Bianucci, Riccardo Mannella

item.title: Local Convergence of Triadic Closures of Sparse Random Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.39535v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Triadic closure is a natural mechanism for modeling the clustering phenomenon observed in many real-world networks. Given a possibly random undirected graph $H$, we consider pairs of non-adjacent vertices that have a common neighbor. Conditional on $H$, each such pair is joined by an edge independently and simultaneously, with a probability depending on the degrees of its endpoints and on the number of their common neighbors. The resulting graph is called a triadic closure of $H$. We study the effect of this operation on local convergence. More precisely, we prove that if a sequence of potentially random finite undirected graphs of $\left( H_n \right)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ converges locally in probability to a rooted graph $H^*$, then the corresponding sequence of triadic closures converges locally in probability to the same triadic closure of $H^*$. As a consequence, we obtain a general limit theorem for the clustering coefficients of triadic closures. In particular, we show that the triadic closures can have a strictly positive limiting clustering coefficients even when the limiting clustering coefficients of the parent graph sequence is zero. Finally, we apply our results to several classical sparse random graph models including Erd\H{o}s-R\'{e}nyi, configuration, preferential attachment models and compute the limiting clustering coefficients of their triadic closures.
item.dc:creator: Himasish Talukdar

item.title: Sharp Tilting Inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2610.39598v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For positive semidefinite matrices $A,B$ and $1/2\le\alpha\le1$, we establish $\operatorname{Tr}\!\left[A\,D\log(A^\alpha+B^\alpha)(B^\alpha)\right] \le s^s(1-s)^{1-s}\operatorname{Tr}[A^\alpha B^{1-\alpha}]$, where $s=(1-\alpha)/\alpha$, with the optimal coefficient. The proof uses a superoperator representation of the directional derivative of the logarithm and an Araki-type estimate for the derivative of a fractional power. Both this inequality and its symmetric-quotient counterpart extend to positive trace-class $A$ and positive, possibly unbounded, self-adjoint $B$ on a separable Hilbert space.
item.dc:creator: Hao-Chung Cheng, Po-Chieh Liu

item.title: Unified transform method for nonautonomous linear evolution equations: rigorous analysis and qualitative theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.39698v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Established herein is the rigorous extension of the celebrated Fokas unified transform method for linear evolution PDE with time-dependent coefficients. As illustrative examples, considered below and rigorously analysed in detail are non-homogeneous initial-boundary-value problems, formulated on the half-line, for the heat equation and the modified heat (also widely known as Barenblatt's pseudo-parabolic) equation with reaction terms and temporally varying coefficients. Solution formulae are derived formally via suitable implementation of the UTM, and rigorously verified a posteriori, in the classical sense. The latter task relies on complex-analytic tools and careful interpretation of the obtained integral representations. The explicit solutions established here are then used for investigating qualitative properties. These include regularity, boundary behavior near the axes of the domain as well as long-range and eventual periodicity asymptotics. Notably, smoothness of the solution up to the boundaries depends on compatibility conditions between initial, boundary and forcing data, into which interjected now are initial values of the coefficients. Further results pertaining to solution uniqueness, analyticity and controllability of the addressed problems are thence deduced in light of the preceding qualitative theory.
item.dc:creator: Andreas Chatziafratis, Spyridon Kamvissis, Alain Miranville, Tohru Ozawa

item.title: Going deep, reaching further: What can Boltzmann machines efficiently represent?
item.description: arXiv:2610.39731v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: While universal approximation theorems theoretically underpin the representation capabilities of machine learning models, they have two shortcomings: They do not focus on efficient representations and they tend to be insensitive to depth and other heuristically important properties. In this work we show that these two shortcomings are intertwined. We prove that machine learning models which are deeper or have higher-order interactions can efficiently represent a larger set of functions, i.e. have larger efficient reach. It follows that deep Boltzmann machines (DBMs) have maximal efficient reach, restricted Boltzmann machines (RBMs) sub-maximal, and k-body generalizations of RBMs form a hierarchy between the two, even though all are universal. More generally, (i) we provide a full characterization of machine learning models with maximal efficient reach; (ii) we derive separations between deep and shallow models for three representation tasks; and (iii) we prove that the efficient reach of shallow models constitutes an infinite hierarchy indexed by the interaction order. The proofs draw on different methodologies, namely on (i) a recent characterization of universal spin models; (ii) computational complexity bounds for spin models; and (iii) communication complexity bounds applied to shallow models. This work shows that universal machine learning models can strongly differ in their efficient representation capabilities, and provides a theoretical foundation for heuristic observations.
item.dc:creator: Tobias Reinhart, Gemma De les Coves

item.title: High-temperature expansion of the inverse-square Ising chain in a magnetic field: exact coefficients and finite-size reconstruction
item.description: arXiv:2610.39815v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The one-dimensional Ising chain with inverse-square interactions is a paradigmatic long-range system: it exhibits the unusual Thouless transition, with a discontinuity in the spontaneous magnetization, yet its full field-dependent thermodynamics remains unknown in closed form. We develop the high-temperature expansion of its free energy while retaining the dependence on a uniform magnetic field at every order. We prove that, after a natural rescaling of the coupling, each coefficient is a rational polynomial in the squared hyperbolic tangent of the reduced field. Remarkably, at each order $n$ the field-dependent free-energy coefficient of a finite, periodically repeated ring is an exact polynomial of degree at most $n$ in $L^{-2}$. The infinite-chain coefficient is its constant term and can therefore be reconstructed from $n+1$ finite rings without numerical extrapolation. Using this reconstruction, we determine the full field-dependent expansion through order 26: 26 polynomials containing 377 rational coefficient entries. We further derive exact formulas, valid at every order, for the coefficients of the two highest powers of the field variable using matching determinants and a cycle-Laplacian reduction. These results reveal an unexpected algebraic structure in the microscopic thermodynamics of the inverse-square chain and provide high-order information about its magnetic response.
item.dc:creator: M. A. Rajabpour

item.title: Moments of characteristic polynomials at random matrix Gram points
item.description: arXiv:2610.39856v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We evaluate the characteristic polynomial of a random unitary matrix at the points on the unit circle where the polynomial takes real values. In analogy to the Riemann zeta function we call these the ``random matrix Gram points''. On the random matrix side we answer in the affirmative a question of Richard Hall, who expected that zeta on the Gram points should be larger than typical. We prove that for any fixed positive $k$, the $2k$th moment of the characteristic polynomial averaged over the random matrix Gram points is larger than the $2k$th moment of the characteristic polynomial averaged over the whole unit circle. For large $N$ the leading-order asymptotic term is the same size, but all lower-order terms are larger. In an appendix we show how to adapt the heuristic recipe of Conrey--Farmer--Keating--Rubinstein--Snaith to conjecture moments of zeta at Gram points, and show by example that the second and fourth moments calculated by following the recipe agree with previously proven results.
item.dc:creator: Christopher Hughes, Somin Kim

item.title: The S-function at arbitrary order: hyperplanes of symmetries and the realisability condition
item.description: arXiv:2610.40033v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a scalar equation $y^{(n)}=\varphi(x,y,\dots,y^{(n-1)})$ the $S$-function of the extended Prelle--Singer method is a vector $S=(S_0,\dots,S_{n-2})$, the null-form vector of Chandrasekar, Senthilvelan, Lakshmanan and collaborators, and the jet gradient of a first integral solves the adjoint of the variational equation. We describe the solutions of the system satisfied by $S$ intrinsically, and determine which of them come from first integrals. Over the field $C$ of first integrals the solutions are exactly the hyperplanes of the $n$-dimensional space $VV$ of symmetry characteristics, recovered from $n-1$ independent characteristics by a Pl\"ucker formula; in flow-box coordinates they are the hyperplane fields on the local space of leaves. A solution is the $S$-vector of a first integral if and only if the corresponding hyperplane field is integrable. This Frobenius condition splits into the $S$-system itself plus $\binom n3$ further differential conditions, so it is vacuous for $n=2$ and a genuine restriction for every $n\ge3$, for which we give an explicit non-realisable solution. The same picture explains why $\lambda$-symmetries and $S$-functions coincide only when $n=2$: line fields and hyperplane fields agree only on surfaces. For the computation of $S$ we record that the system is equivalent to one scalar equation for the last component, which is the Riccati form of the adjoint variational equation, and we spell out what this does and does not imply for a rational search.
item.dc:creator: L. G. S. Duarte, L. A. C. P. da Mota

item.title: Degenerate complex structures on surfaces and stability conditions
item.description: arXiv:2610.40035v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Physical heuristics suggest that the space of Bridgeland stability conditions of a projective Calabi-Yau manifold $X$ should be related to the moduli space of complex structures on its mirror $X^\vee$. On the other hand, recent work in the literature introduces a modular partial compactification, $\mathcal{A}\mathrm{Stab}(X)$, of a quotient of the space of stability conditions on $\mathcal{D}^{b}(X)$. We provide some mathematical evidence for the aforementioned heuristics by proving that for curves and surfaces, certain boundary strata in $\mathcal{A}\mathrm{Stab}(X)$ describe degenerate complex structures on $X^\vee$. Along the way, we introduce a criterion for producing boundary points of $\mathcal{A}\mathrm{Stab}(\mathcal{D})$ when $\mathcal{D}$ is an arbitrary $k$-linear triangulated category. As a byproduct, we deduce the existence of Bridgeland stability conditions on certain quotients of the derived categories of K3 and Enriques surfaces.
