item.title: Discrete Mixed Quantization for Cat Maps
item.description: arXiv:2609.32113v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we develop a mixed quantization technique for graph vector bundles that combines semiclassical analysis and quantum cat maps. We apply it to study the Kesten--McKay law and quantum ergodicity.
item.dc:creator: Elena Kim, Qiaochu Ma

item.title: Uniqueness of four-body convex central configurations for all masses
item.description: arXiv:2609.35632v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that for every choice of four positive masses and every cyclic ordering of the bodies there is exactly one strictly convex planar central configuration with that ordering, up to similarity. This proves a conjecture of Albouy, Fu and Sun, also called the Sim\'o-Yoccoz conjecture, and answers Problem 10 in the list of Albouy, Cabral and Santos. Uniqueness follows by a covering argument from the nondegeneracy of these configurations. We prove nondegeneracy by hand: Dziobek's relations reduce it to an eigenvalue bound for a $2\times2$ matrix that depends only on the shape of the configuration. As consequences, every degenerate planar four-body central configuration is concave, and the known symmetry theorems for kites, isosceles trapezoids and rhombi follow in a few lines.
item.dc:creator: Tejasvi Singh Tomar

item.title: Liquid crystalline order and its impact on shape evolution of fluid lipid membranes
item.description: arXiv:2609.40113v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider extensions of the classical curvature-elasticity free energy for a fluid lipid membrane, explicitly treating the liquid crystal structure of the membrane, which results from the lipid molecules that are, on average, oriented normal to the surface. Locally varying liquid crystal order leads to local variations in bending rigidities and surface viscosity and thus influences the shape evolution. This provides a multiscale coupling between the local membrane mechanics on the level of the lipids and the mesoscopic length and time scales of biological functions. Numerical simulations in the one-constant approximation demonstrate the impact of local membrane mechanics on the emerging equilibrium shapes. These shapes not only depend on the specified conserved surface area and enclosed volume, as for the classical curvature-elasticity free energy, but also the elastic parameter and are characterized by a reduced liquid crystal order at highly curved regions. The modified shapes and their varying liquid crystal order, as function of curvature, provide experimentally testable properties. Exploring the dynamic evolution demonstrate a tight coupling of tangential flow, shape evolution and liquid crystalline order. We further point to model extensions towards lipid phase separation and asymmetric lipid bilayers and biological implications.
item.dc:creator: Ingo Nitschke, Maik Porrmann, Axel Voigt

item.title: Classification of commutation relation for multi-chordal SLE
item.description: arXiv:2610.04362v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We classify the linear solution spaces of the chordal Belavin--Polyakov--Zamolodchikov (BPZ) equations, which arise in Dub\'edat's commutation relations for multiple Schramm--Loewner evolutions (SLE). Without imposing growth conditions, we determine the subspaces selected by successive conformal Ward identities and their exact dimensions. For every $\kappa>0$ and BPZ spectral parameter $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}$, we determine the spectrum and Jordan structure of the translation operator. When $\lambda=0$ and $\kappa\in(0,8)$, we further determine all admissible scaling exponents and the dimensions of the corresponding translation-invariant solution spaces. A triangular change of derivative coordinates yields a first-order system of rational Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov type, allowing us to represent the Ward operators explicitly and reduce the classification to finite-dimensional linear algebra. For $2N$ boundary points and $\kappa\in(0,8)$, translation-invariant BPZ solutions with $\lambda=0$ and the homogeneity required by M\"obius covariance automatically satisfy the third Ward identity and the usual power-law bound. This recovers, under weaker assumptions, the Catalan dimension formula previously established by Flores and Kleban. At $\kappa=8$, the third Ward identity imposes an additional constraint when $N\ge2$, but the full M\"obius-covariant solution space still has Catalan dimension, establishing completeness of the partition functions constructed from uniform spanning trees. Finally, at $\kappa=4$ and $\lambda>0$, we construct an explicit basis of positive BPZ solutions and identify its elements as partition functions for level lines of a Gaussian free field with suitable harmonic means.
item.dc:creator: Mo Chen, Chongzhi Huang, Hao Wu

item.title: Adiabatic tracking and geometric schedules for classical and quantum Gibbs-state preparation
item.description: arXiv:2610.06268v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a discrete adiabatic framework for Gibbs-state preparation in classical and quantum optimisation algorithms. For finite time-inhomogeneous reversible Markov chains, we derive a tracking theorem that bounds the distance between the evolving distribution and the instantaneous stationary state. The bound combines contraction of accumulated error with the new error generated as the stationary distribution changes. For Gibbs paths, it yields explicit step-complexity bounds and an effective tracking metric determined by the spectral gap and equilibrium energy fluctuations. The associated constant-speed schedule minimizes the metric-energy functional and, in the small-gap regime, takes the form $\dot\beta\propto\delta(\beta)/V(\beta)$, where $V(\beta)=\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}_{\pi_\beta}(E)}$. We then apply the discrete quantum adiabatic theorem to temperature-dependent Szegedy quantum walks, whose eigenphase gap satisfies $\Delta_w=\Theta(\sqrt{\delta_+})$, with $\delta_+$ the underlying Markov kernel's right spectral gap. Under uniform bounds on the discrete operator variation and suitable spectral and path-integral assumptions, gap-adapted schedules give a sufficient fixed-accuracy cost of $O(\delta_{+,\min}^{-1/2})$. This gives a quadratic improvement in gap dependence relative to the classical inverse-gap relaxation scale under the stated assumptions. Numerical tests on a solvable two-state model and Sherrington-Kirkpatrick instances compare tracking and final preparation errors and investigate the transfer of schedules from smaller to larger systems.
item.dc:creator: Pedro C. S. Costa, Mauro E. S. Morales, Dong An, Kaur Kristjuhan

item.title: Projected Yang-Mills Theory and the MacDowell-Mansouri Analogy
item.description: arXiv:2610.08566v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct Yang-Mills theories with projected curvature kinetic terms, developing their analogy with MacDowell-Mansouri gravity and their connection to nonlinear sigma models. We begin with models exhibiting explicit symmetry breaking and use them to motivate gauge-covariant Higgs extensions. For $SO(2n)$, an orthogonal complex structure defines a degenerate kinetic operator with image $\mathfrak{su}(n)$, while the adjoint Higgs vacuum has stabilizer $U(n)$. We compare the fixed-projector theory with gauge-covariant formulations involving either unrestricted adjoint Higgs fields or Higgs fields constrained exactly to the orbit $SO(2n)/U(n)$. We express the Stelle-West Higgs-gravity action through a single Clifford involution whose complementary projectors select the Lorentz curvature, isolate the radial Higgs derivative, and construct the induced spacetime metric. This formulation makes the common projector structure explicit and clarifies the distinct roles of curvature projection, the internal dual, and the coframe. In the orbit-constrained Yang-Mills theory with a positive Higgs kinetic coefficient the coset connection is auxiliary and the central connection drops out of the action. A nonlinear Dirac analysis establishes a regular weak-curvature branch with $2(n^2-1)$ physical degrees of freedom in four dimensions, locally equivalent to $SU(n)$ Yang-Mills theory. In the unrestricted theory, normal Higgs displacements can change the kinetic rank, so this degree-of-freedom count does not automatically extend beyond the constrained field space. We also characterize possible nontrivial algebraic branches and introduce projected Pontryagin theories and a full-rank equivariant completion.
item.dc:creator: Pedro D. Alvarez

item.title: Existence and uniqueness of radial bound states with prescribed number of nodes for nonlinear dispersive equations on spherically symmetric manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.13813v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Standing waves $e^{i\omega t}u(x)$ of nonlinear dispersive equations, such as the nonlinear Schr\"odinger and Klein--Gordon equations, have a profile $u$ that solves the semilinear elliptic equation $\Delta u+f(u)=0$. We prove the existence of radial bound states with a prescribed number of nodal surfaces for this equation on a large class of spherically symmetric manifolds and for a broad class of nonlinearities $f$. Under further assumptions on the metric, we prove uniqueness of such bound states for the model nonlinearity $f(u)=|u|^{p-1}u-u$. Both existence and uniqueness results apply to the hyperbolic spaces $\mathbb{H}^n_\lambda$ of any curvature $-\lambda^2$ and dimension $n\geq 3$, and to some manifolds with a singularity at the origin.
item.dc:creator: Valentino Badalucco

item.title: Finiteness of planar central configurations of five bodies for all positive masses: On Smale's sixth problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.16107v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Combining local boundary analysis, algebraic curves and the computational statements specified in the appendix, we prove that the planar Newtonian five-body problem has finitely many central configurations up to rotation, translation and scaling for every choice of positive masses. This gives the five-body statement of Smale's sixth problem. We use the singular-sequence classification of Albouy and Kaloshin and resolve the corresponding boundary equations through weighted blow-up charts, rank calculations and local compatibility conditions. For the two remaining diagrams, we prove that the product $\Delta$ of all squared mutual distances vanishes. On a hypothetical solution curve containing a positive arc, a pole of a four-product therefore gives a zero of $\Delta$. A pole of $\Delta$ elsewhere on the completed curve, together with $\Delta^4=\prod_{i<j}p_{ij}$, then contradicts the same local vanishing result. The computational statements for Diagrams~2, 3 and~6 involve exact algebra, interval arithmetic and ball arithmetic.
item.dc:creator: Zhe Chen, Zhicheng Tong

item.title: Beyond the lemon: Spectra of random Lindblad operators with a Hamiltonian component
item.description: arXiv:2610.19261v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Generators of continuous-time quantum Markovian evolution, known as Lindblad operators, play a key role in the theory of open quantum systems. The question of how to define and characterize random Lindblad operators has attracted considerable attention in recent years. Purely dissipative random Lindbladians have been extensively studied using toolboxes of free probability and non-Hermitian random matrix theories, which helped to uncover a characteristic lemon-like spectral support. In this work, we focus on random Lindbladians with a Hamiltonian component. We analyze three ensembles of increasing complexity, designed to illustrate the joint effects of dissipative and Hamiltonian dynamics. While the first two allow for an exact analytic treatment with standard probabilistic and scalar-valued free-probability methods, the most general case requires the more general framework of operator-valued free probability. We explain how the spectral support changes with the relative Hamiltonian strength and the rank of the dissipative component and characterize the effect of Hamiltonian-induced spectral squeezing.
item.dc:creator: Mykhailo Hontarenko, Wojciech Tarnowski, Sergey Denisov, Karol \.Zyczkowski

item.title: Difference between pair creation and anomaly matching: Nontrivial aspects of invertible symmetries and defects in $SU(N)$ models
item.description: arXiv:2610.21478v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the connection between the $SU(N)_{K}$ Wess-Zumino-Witten (WZW) model and $SU(N)_{K'}$ WZW model, enforcing the $\mathbb{Z}_{N}$ symmetries. The fundamental underlying structures are the (half-)integer spin simple currents in the topological quantum field theories and anomaly matching conditions in conformal field theories. For the (half-)integer spin simple current condition, we obtain the generalized pairing condition $K= \pm R^{2}K' (\text{mod}.N)$ with $\text{gcd}(R,N)=1$. On the other hand, the anomaly matching condition results in the weaker condition $K= \pm RUK' (\text{mod}.N)$ with $\text{gcd}(R,N)=\text{gcd}(U,N)=1$. The preservation law of the $\mathbb{Z}_{N}$ defects and symmetries is compatible only with the pairing condition.
item.dc:creator: Yoshiki Fukusumi, Shuma Nakashiba

item.title: Group averaging and the geometry of physical quantum states: from normalizable solutions to solvable loop quantum cosmology
item.description: arXiv:2610.24027v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In canonical quantum gravity the physical states solve the constraints but are typically not normalizable in the kinematical Hilbert space. Group averaging constructs them from normalizable kinematical seeds. We describe the geometry of this seed-to-state map in the language of geometric quantum mechanics. When averaging is an orthogonal projection, the admissible kinematical rays form a holomorphic vector bundle over the physical ray space. The embedded exact solutions form its zero section, and its fibers are strictly larger than gauge orbits. Observables descend to the base exactly when the Hessian of the squared constraint vanishes along their flow. For distributional physical states, group averaging on an explicit Sobolev test space yields an affine bundle of representatives. Its sections are embeddings of the physical ray space whose images contain no exact solutions. The test-space inner product singles out one of them, and narrowing the seed profile gives Weyl sequences of approximate solutions. We apply this to solvable loop quantum cosmology. Group averaging reproduces the Klein--Gordon physical inner product on an explicit test space. Because the scalar-field momentum enters the constraint quadratically, the constraint spectrum has an edge near the shell. The canonical section is then mode-dependent and not K\"ahler isometric, and the canonical seeds of small universes are biased off the shell. The edge also separates the Page--Wootters state from the slice of the Klein--Gordon solution. An ideal clock shows none of these effects. The results separate the canonical structures, namely physical rays, physical geometry and Dirac observables, from those that depend on a choice of seeds, test space or clock.
item.dc:creator: Alejandro Corichi

item.title: Nonlocal Equations on Domains and Manifolds Without Symmetries
item.description: arXiv:2610.28572v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work, we establish existence and regularity results for solutions to nonlinear nonlocal equations of the form $f(\Delta)u = U(x,u)$ and $f(\Delta_{g})u = U(x,u)$ in Euclidean and Riemannian settings, respectively. We prove existence results across three distinct geometric scenarios: bounded domains in $\mathbb{R}^n$, perturbed equations on compact Riemannian manifolds, and noncompact Cartan-Hadamard manifolds under suitable geometric curvature conditions.
item.dc:creator: Santiago Castellanos
